q: When a charge is given to a conducting object of any shape, the charge is found to be spread out over the _____ surface of the object.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. When a charge is given to a conducting object of any shape, the charge is found to be spread out over the outer surface of the object. Inner or middle is not this quantity.

q: The charge on a conducting object is not uniformly distributed; the more highly curved parts have a _____ concentration of charge.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The charge on a conducting object is not uniformly distributed; the more highly curved parts have a greater concentration of charge. Do not trade greater for lesser or zero.

q: Charges are highly concentrated at the _____ portion of the object.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. Charges are highly concentrated at the pointed portion of the object. Flat or curved is not this quantity.

q: A pointed rod is very useful as a _____ because the charge concentration at the pointed end is so large that some charges leak off into the air.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. A pointed rod is very useful as a lightning conductor because the charge concentration at the pointed end is so large that some charges leak off into the air. Capacitor or insulator is not this quantity.

q: The electric field is _____ everywhere inside a charged conducting object of any shape.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The electric field is zero everywhere inside a charged conducting object of any shape. Maximum or uniform is not this quantity.

q: The motion of charges or the current is not observed in a charged conducting object because there is no _____ inside it.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The motion of charges or the current is not observed in a charged conducting object because there is no electric field inside it. Do not trade electric field for magnetic field or potential difference.

q: If the electric field intensity varies from point to point in an electric field, such an electric field is called a _____ electric field.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. If the electric field intensity varies from point to point in an electric field, such an electric field is called a non-uniform electric field. Uniform or static is not this quantity.

q: The electric field around a point charge is an example of a _____ electric field.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The electric field around a point charge is an example of a non-uniform electric field. Do not trade non-uniform for uniform or parallel.

q: If the electric field intensity at every point is the same in magnitude and direction, such an electric field is called a _____ electric field.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. If the electric field intensity at every point is the same in magnitude and direction, such an electric field is called a uniform electric field. Do not trade uniform for non-uniform or radial.

q: The electric field between two oppositely charged parallel plates is a _____ electric field.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The electric field between two oppositely charged parallel plates is a uniform electric field. Non-uniform or spherical is not this quantity.

q: For a charged pointed rod, the charge concentration at the pointed end is so large that some of the charges _____ off into the air.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. For a charged pointed rod, the charge concentration at the pointed end is so large that some of the charges leak off into the air. Do not trade leak for flow or jump.

q: The electric lines of force which represent a non-uniform electric field are not parallel but are continuous _____.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The electric lines of force which represent a non-uniform electric field are not parallel but are continuous curves. Do not trade curves for lines or circles.

q: A uniform electric field is represented by electric lines of force which are uniformly spaced _____ lines of the same length.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. A uniform electric field is represented by electric lines of force which are uniformly spaced parallel lines of the same length. Curved or intersecting is not this quantity.

q: The charge distribution on a conductor depends on the _____ of the object.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The charge distribution on a conductor depends on the shape of the object. Mass or color is not this quantity.
